text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make software easier to understand and maintain. When developers refactor, they often simplify complex functions, remove duplicate code, and give variables clearer names. These changes improve readability, so other programmers can work with the code more easily. Refactoring also helps reduce technical debt, which builds up when quick fixes are used instead of proper solutions. Although refactoring takes time, it saves effort in the long run because cleaner code is less likely to contain bugs and is cheaper to update.
